title: Newton’s method
goal: Zero in on solutions to $f(x) = 0$ that algebra cannot solve by repeatedly sliding down the tangent line: $x_{n+1} = x_n - \frac{f(x_n)}{f'(x_n)}$.

beforeThis.skill: Where does the formula come from? Draw the tangent line at $(x_n, f(x_n))$, set $y = 0$ to find where it hits the $x$-axis, and solve for $x_{n+1}$!

links.label: Precalculus: Equations of lines and x-intercepts

seeIt.title: Newton-Raphson Idea
seeIt.creator: Mathematical Visual Proofs
seeIt.watchFor: One-minute visual picture of how riding tangent lines to the x-axis converges to a root.

questions.asking: Compute $x_1$ and $x_2$ starting from $x_0 = 3$ for $f(x) = x^2 - 10$, leaving $x_2$ in calculator-ready form.
questions.statement: Starting at $x_0 = 3$, use two iterations of Newton’s method to approximate the root of $f(x) = x^2 - 10$. You may leave your answer in calculator-ready form.

Starting at $x_0 = 3$, use one iteration of Newton’s method to approximate the root of $f(x) = x^3 - 30$. Express your answer as a simplified fraction. Then, check that you’re on the right path by cubing your answer with a calculator.

questions.asking: Apply two iterations to the derivative equation $g'(x) = 0$ (starting from a simple nearby guess such as $x_0 = 0$) to approximate the critical point of $g(x) = x - x^2 - x^4$.
questions.statement: Use two iterations of Newton’s method to approximate the $x$-value of the critical point of the function $g(x) = x - x^2 - x^4$.

questions.asking: Compute $x_1$ and $x_2$ starting at $x_0 = 2$ for $f(x) = x^3 - 12x + 15$, leaving $x_2$ in calculator-ready form.
questions.statement:
Use two iterations of Newton’s method to approximate a root of the function

$$f(x) = x^3 - 12x + 15$$

close to $x = 2$. Leave your answer in calculator-ready form.

questions.asking: Write a polynomial equation $f(x) = 0$ whose positive root is $\sqrt{8}$, pick the closest integer starting guess $x_0$, and perform one step to get a rational approximation.
questions.statement: Use one iteration of Newton’s method to find an approximate value for $\sqrt{8}$ that is a rational number. (Hint: first think of a function, $f(x)$, such that $f(x) = 0$ has the solution $x = \sqrt{8}$.)

questions.asking: The root of $x^3 - 2 = 0$ sits between two integers. Decide which of those integers is the closer start, and say why, before you iterate.
questions.statement: December 2024 final. We want a rational approximation of $\sqrt[3]{2}$, thought of as a solution of $x^3 - 2 = 0$. Starting from an integer, find consecutive integers that bracket the root. Which one is likely closer, and why?
